correctness.rationale: Proposition 2.8 of the primary source gives the complete irredundant facet list in the stated regime. At the proposed diagonal center, coordinate and total-sum facet distances both equal the displayed radius. For every proper k-subset facet, the required crossing value h_k is the restriction of a one-variable function whose derivative numerator is strictly decreasing, so its minimum occurs at an endpoint. Both endpoint crossing values are proved strictly larger than the candidate radius. Finally, any inscribed ball must satisfy q_i>=rho and sum(q_i)+rho*sqrt(m)<=T_n; summing gives the matching upper bound, and equality forces every q_i=rho, proving uniqueness.

value.rationale: Partial permutohedra are an actively studied two-parameter family connecting generalized permutohedra, anti-blocking polytopes, stellohedra, and parking-function polytopes. The source explicitly identifies the m>n regime as structurally different and harder for several enumerative invariants. The theorem gives a complete metric classification precisely in the previously uncovered redundant range: despite the surviving proper subset facets, the inball is exactly the simplex-envelope inball, with a unique center and complete contact set. This is an all-parameter structural statement, not a low-dimensional or arbitrary slice computation.
